 Tiger Woods set to design new golf course in Northern Ireland
 Updated / Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
 15:19
 Getty
 Tiger Woods will design the new course 
 Tiger Woods has confirmed he will design the first championship-standard links golf course built in Northern Ireland for more than 100 years, describing the project as a "special opportunity".
 Reports linking the 15-time major champion with the proposed £30 million (€35.8m) course at Bellarena on the north-west coast between Limavady and Coleraine had been circulating for several weeks ahead of Thursday's official announcement.
 "Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team," said Woods.
 "We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it."
 Hospitality group Galgorm Collection is building the course, with construction set to get under way next year if the required planning approvals are secured.
 The company already owns and runs the championship parkland course at Galgorm Castle in Ballymena and a course at Roe Valley in Limavady.
 Bellarena is around 28 kilometres from Open championship venue Royal Portrush Golf Club. Nearby Portstewart and Castlerock also boast acclaimed links courses.
 Galgorm Collection is collaborating on the project with Reef Destinations, which specialises in golf resorts.
 Colin Johnston, chief executive of Galgorm Collection, announced that Woods and his TGR Design firm would craft the new links layout.
 "Supported by Reef Destinations, Tiger Woods and TGR Design, we're delighted to be significantly advancing our plans to create an outstanding championship links course at Bellarena," he said.
 "Set against the spectacular backdrop of Northern Ireland's rugged north-west coast, our plans represent a once-in-a-generation opportunity to transform Northern Ireland's golfing and tourism future.
 "This exciting, landmark development will build on our internationally acclaimed reputation as a world-class golf destination, attract new visitors, drive significant economic growth and create hundreds of jobs for the local community."
 Reef Destinations has previously worked with TGR Design on course construction projects in the US.
Bellarena already has a historical link with the United States, as it was the site of an US Army base during the Second World War.
 "Northern Ireland is an important part of the golf world, and very few people ever get to be a part of something this special," said Jared Lucero, chief executive of Reef Capital Partners, the operators of Reef Destinations.
 "Creating the kind of experience this place deserves requires great partners.
 "Galgorm Collection has represented Irish hospitality for 30 years, and pairing that with Tiger and the TGR Design team is something we're proud to be part of.
 "We want to build a place golfers will travel the world for, and that this community will be proud of for generations."
